strings.name: Piyush Gupta
strings.role: Former DBS CEO, Keppel Non-Executive Chairman and Council of Presidential Advisers Member
strings.summary: Piyush Gupta worked in Asian banking at Citi before leading DBS from 2009 to 2025. He advanced digital banking and regional expansion, while his tenure also saw regulatory restrictions following service disruptions. After leaving DBS, he joined Keppel’s board, becoming Non-Executive Chairman in 2026, and became a full member of Singapore’s Council of Presidential Advisers.
strings.coverageNote: Checked through 17 November 2026. Former DBS duties are separated from non-executive Keppel roles, and alternate from full council membership. Operational difficulties during digital transformation are retained; the postgraduate management diploma is not relabeled an MBA.
strings.influence.rationale: Led DBS for many years, advancing banking digitalization and regional business expansion in Asia.
strings.facts.f1.label: Education
strings.facts.f1.value: Earned a BA (Honours) in Economics from St. Stephen’s College, Delhi University, and a Post Graduate Diploma in Management from IIM Ahmedabad.
strings.facts.f2.label: Changing roles
strings.facts.f2.value: Retired as DBS CEO and Executive Director on 28 March 2025; became Keppel’s independent Non-Executive Chairman on 17 April 2026 and a full presidential advisory council member on 2 June.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Digital banking practice
strings.highlights.h1.text: Promoted transformation through redesigned customer journeys, employee experimentation and technology learning; repeated service disruptions nevertheless led to regulatory restrictions in 2023.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Expanding in India
strings.highlights.h2.text: During his DBS tenure, Lakshmi Vilas Bank was amalgamated into DBS Bank India in 2020 under a government and central-bank statutory scheme.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Becomes presidential advisory council member
strings.timeline.t1.text: Moved from alternate to full membership, appointed on the Chief Justice’s advice.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Becomes Keppel Non-Executive Chairman
strings.timeline.t2.text: Succeeded Danny Teoh following re-election at the AGM, as an independent non-executive director.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Joins Keppel’s board
strings.timeline.t3.text: Became Deputy Chairman and an independent non-executive director, not yet Board Chairman.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Retires as DBS CEO and director
strings.timeline.t4.text: Retired at the conclusion of the AGM, ending the tenure begun in 2009.
strings.timeline.t5.title: DBS faces regulatory restrictions
strings.timeline.t5.text: Following repeated service disruptions, MAS imposed measures including a six-month pause on non-essential IT changes at the bank.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Indian bank amalgamation takes effect
strings.timeline.t6.text: Lakshmi Vilas Bank merged into DBS Bank India under a statutory scheme, before the 30 November completion announcement.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Becomes DBS CEO
strings.timeline.t7.text: Began leading DBS Group and DBS Bank; the September announcement date is not his start date.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Begins Citi career
strings.timeline.t8.text: Subsequently held various Asian banking roles; the biography separately records a return to Citi in 2001, so service was not uninterrupted.
